Amanda Silberling
Microsoft will lay off 9,000 employees, or less
than 4% of the company
Microsoft is planning to lay off 9,000 employees, impacting less than 4% of its global workforce,
according to a report by CNBC.
Microsoft continues to beat expectations in its quarterly earnings; in its most recent report, the
company grew its net income by 18% year over year, amounting to a total of $25.8 billion.
However, the company has continued to reduce its headcount — this is one of many rounds of
layoffs to have already occurred this year.
Microsoft has said that these cuts are an attempt to cut down on its layers of management, following
the lead of competitors like Amazon and Meta.
